Judgment:
1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954
(herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused have violated the provisions of t
he PFA Act and Rules.

2. As per the complaint, on 08.08.2002, the Food Inspector (herein after referred to as FI) Sh D.P.
Singh and FI N.N. Sharma under the supervision of Local Health Authority (herein after referred to DA vs Chander Kumar etc as LHA)/SDM Sh G.R. Meena visited the premises of M/s Shyamlal &
Brothers, Shop No. 1752, Nai Basti, S.P. Mukherjee Marg, Delhi, where the accused Chander Kumar was found conducting the business in the above mention shop, having stored various food articles including "Kuber Readymade Scented Khaini" for sale for human consumption.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of "Kuber Readymade Scented Khaini"
from the vendor for analysis.
The sample consisted 6 X 250 gms sealed polythene packets of "Kuber Readymade scented Khaini" taken as such bearing label declaration as mentioned in form-VI.
The sample was taken under the supervision/direction of Sh. G.R. Meena, SDM/LHA.
The Food Inspector divided the sample then and there into three parts.
Each counter part containing the sample was separately packed fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules.
The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample counter parts.
Notice was given to accused No. 1 Chander Kumar and the price of sample was also given to him vide vendor receipt dated 8-8-2002.
Panchnama too was prepared at the spot.
All the documents prepared by F.I. were signed by accused No. 1 Chander Kumar and the other witness Sh. N.N. Shanna, FI.

Before starting sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such Sh. N.N. Shanna, FI was joined as witness.

2 3.
One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA code No. GRM/LHA/002145 was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and two counter-pans were deposited with the LHA in intact condition.
Public Analyst analysed the sample and found DA vs Chander Kumar etc the Khaini to be conforming to the standards but sweetened supari is adulterated.

entities.text: DA vs Chander Kumar etc the Khaini

sentences.text:
The report of the Public Analyst is as follows:
"The sample of scented khaini is not adulterated but sweetened supari is adulterated because it is coloured with synthetic colouring matter viz. Tartrazine use of colour is not allowed in supari.
Supari pouch is also misbranded as the declaration for colour & artificial sweeterner are not made as per the requirement of Rule-24 and Rule-42 ZZZ(1).

4. At the time of analysing the sample Public Analyst found that "Kuber Ready made scented khaini sample in original sealed small pouches of 10 grns. each, 25 such pouches are contained in another original polythene packet with declaration of one free pouch whose details are not given on this packet complies with Rule-32" and alter analysis opined vide report number PFA/Enf.1277/2002 dated 3-9-2002 that the sample of scented khaini is not adulterated but sweetened supari is adulterated because it is coloured with synthetic colouring matter viz. Tartrazine use of colour is not allowed in supari.
Supari pouch is also misbranded as the declaration for colour & artificial sweeterner are not made as per the requirement of Rule-24 and Rule-42 ZZZ(1).
5. It is the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 Chander Kumar was the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Shyam Lal & Brothers, Shop No.1752.
Nai Basti.
S.P. Muhherjee Marg, Delhi-6 at the time of sampling and is in charge of and responsible for the day to day conduct of the business of the said shop.

The sampled DA vs Chander Kumar etc food article has been purchased by the vendor from M/s New Delhi Marketing Co., A-145, Ganesh Nagar, New Delhi-18 which is a proprietorship concern and accused No. 2 Smt. Suman Khatter is the proprietor of the concern and as such she is in charge of and responsible for the day to day conduct of the said business.
Accused No.2 Smt. Suman Khatter has disclosed that the sampled food article was purchased from accused No.3 M/s Kuber Khaini Private Private Ltd, 32, K, Siraspur, GT Kamal Road, Delhi-42.

Accused No. 3 M/s Kuber Khaini Private Ltd. had appointed accused No. 4 Hari Rain Production Manager as its nominee under the PFA Act at the time of sampling & as such the nominee accused No. 4 Hari Ram and the company are liable and responsible for the day to day conduct of the said business.
6.

It is further stated that accused No. 3 M/s Kuber Khaini Pvt. Ltd. disclosed that free pouches of Supari which were packed along with the "Kuber ready made scented Khaini" were purchased from accused No.5 M/s Kuber Grains & Spices Pvt. Ltd. Khasra No. 1282, Kapashera Village, New Delhi-110037.
Accused No.5 M/s Kuber Grains & Spieces P Ltd. is having two directors namely accused No.6 Raj Kumar Malu and accused No.7 Lakshmi Pati Jain.
As there was no nominee appointed by the company at the time of sampling both the directors are responsible along with the company for the day to day conduct of the said business.

3 7.
Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA.

The complaint was then filed in the court on 03.11.2003 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(j)(m) and section 2(ix)(k) of PFA Rules, DA vs Chander Kumar etc 1955 as well as Rule 23 read with Rule 28 & 29 and Rule 24 & 42 ZZZ(1) of PFA Rules 1955 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused.
8. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 07.11.2001.

Based on the report of the PA charge was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia)(j)(m), Section 2(ix(k) of PFA Act 1954 and Rule 23 read with Rule 28 & 29 of PFA Rules, Rule 24 and 42 (ZZZ)(1) of PFA Rule 1955,
to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
9.
At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI Arun Kumar, PW-2 FI N.N. Sharma and PW- 3 SDM/LHA Sh G.R. Meena.
PW-2 and FI Sh D.P. Singh were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh G.R.Meena.

These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of six original sealed polythene packets of 250 gms each of "Kuber Readymade Scented Khaini", bearing identical label declaration from the accused, dividing the sample commodity into three equal parts by putting 2 sealed packets together as one counterpart,
separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses.
They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-2/A, DA vs Chander Kumar etc Notice in Form-VI Ex.PW-2/B and Panchnama Ex.PW-1/D.
The vendor disclosed the source of purchase of sample commodity on the spot and handed over purchase bill Mark X-14.
A notice u/s 14-A Ex.PW2/C was also prepared at the spot addressed to supplier M/s New Delhi Marketing Company.
Thereafter two counterpart of the sample commodity were deposited on the next working day, under intimation that one counterpart of the same has already been deposited with PA.
Thereafter, PA Report Ex.PW3/A was received which revealed that the sample was not adulterated but of sweetned supari was adulterated and was also misbranded.

Thereafter the matter was marked to PW-1 FI Arun Kumar, who on the direction of SDM/LHA started the investigation and sent letter Ex.PW1/A to vendor and received its reply Ex.PW1/A-1 alongwith document Mark-X and X-1.
Thereafter PW-1 FI Arun Kumar sent letter Ex.PW1/B and reminder Ex.PW1/B-1 to New Delhi Marketing company and received its reply Ex.PW1/B-2 alongwith photocopy of bill Mrk X-2.
PW-1 FI Arun Kumar also sent letter Ex.PW1/C to Kuber Khaini P Ltd and received reply Ex.PW1/C-1.
PW-1 FI Arun Kumar again sent letter Ex.PW1/C-2 and reminder Ex.PW1/C-3 to Kuber Khani P Ltd and received reply Ex.PW1/C-4 alongwith photocopy of nomination in Form VIII Mark X-3.

PW-1 FI Arun Kumar also sent letter ExPW1/D to Kuber and received reply Ex.PW1/D-1 alongwith photocopy of nomination in form-VII Mark X-4 and minutes of meeting mark X-5 and photocopy of invoice Mark X-6 to 10.
Thereafter PW-1 FI Arun Kumar verified from PFA office regarding nominee of M/s Kuber Khaini P Ltd vide letter Ex.PW1/E and received reply and document Mark X-11 and X-12 from LHA.

Thereafter on completion of investigation, the entire DA vs Chander Kumar etc case file was sent to concern SDM/LHA who forwarded the then Director, PFA Sh. S.N. Bansal for obtaining his consent for Da vs Chander Kumar Etc on 16 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64226644/
4 prosecution of accused persons and the then Director, PFA after applying his mind granted his consent for prosecution Ex.PW1/F.

Thereafter, the present complaint Ex.PW1/G was filed before the Court and then intimation letter Ex. PW1/H along with copy of PA Report were sent to the accused persons through registered post mark X-13.

These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld.
Defence Counsel.
10. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 10.08.2016 wherein the accused persons denied the allegations and pleaded innocence.
Thereafter the matter was listed for defence evidence.
The accused chose not to lead DE and vide order dated 08.11.2016 the defence evidence was closed and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
11. In a criminal case, the burden is on the prosecution to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt by leading positive evidence.
This burden cannot be shifted to the accused and it has to be necessary discharged by the prosecution itself.
12. The present case alleges adulteration in the sample of Kuber Readymade Scented Khaini collected from the business concern of the accused no.1 .
This sample of Kuber Readymade Scented Khaini has been analysed by the PA.
His report is reproduced above.
13. The whole case of prosecution is based on the PA as the accused DA vs Chander Kumar etc have not exercised their right to get the sample analysed from CFL.

The defence has raised an argument that the complaint was filed after the expiry of the product in question and the defence has relied upon the judgement of of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in State of Haryana vs Unique Farmaid P.
Ltd & Ors 1999 (2) FAC399 to argue that the manufacturing date of Kuber Readymade Scented Khaini 08/2002 and it was best before six months from the date of packing.

entities.text:
State of Haryana vs Unique Farmaid P.
Ltd & Ors 1999 (2) FAC399
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also submitted that date of manufacturing and packing are generally the same or may be immediately after.
The complaint was filed after one year and three months of lifting the sample.
By that time the shelf life of the sample has passed thats why the accused have not exercised their right to get the sample analysed by CFL and it has prejudiced the accused in their defence.
14. I have gone through the judgement citied by the defence.
In this case, the sample in question was of an insecticide.
The manufacturing date of insecticides was March 1994 and its expiry date was February 1995.
By the time the accused was summoned to appear in the Court on April 06, 1995.
they had lost their right of getting the samples be analysed from Central Insecticide Laboratory.

The Hon'ble Court held that by the time, the respondents were asked to appear before the Court, the expiry date of insecticide was already over and sending of sample to the Central Insecticide Laboratory at that stage would be of no consequence.

In the words of Hon'ble Court :-
"Sub-section (1) of Section 30 which appears to be relevant only prescribes in effect that ignorance would be of no defence but that does not mean that if there are contraventions of other mandatory DA vs Chander Kumar etc provisions of the Act,
the accused have no remedy.
Procedure for testing the sample is prescribed and if it is contravened to the prejudice of the accused, he certainly has right to seek dismissal of the complaint.
There cannot be two opinions about that.

Then in order to safeguard Da vs Chander Kumar Etc on 16 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64226644/
5 the right of the accused to have the sample tested from Central Insecticides Laboratory, it is incumbent on the prosecution to file the complaint expeditiously so that the right of the accused is not lost.

In the present case, by the time the respondents were asked to appear before the Court, expiry date of the insecticide was already over and sending of sample to the Central Insecticides Laboratory at that late stage would be of no consequence.
This issue is no longer res integra.

In The State of Punjab v. National Organic Chemical Industries Ltd., JT (1996) 10 SC 480 this Court in somewhat similar circumstances said that the procedure laid down under Section 24 of the Act deprived the accused to have sample tested by the Central Insecticides Laboratory and adduce evidence of the report so given in his defence.

entities.text: State of Punjab v. National Organic Chemical Industries Ltd., JT (1996) 10 SC 480
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court stressed the need to lodge the complaint with utmost dispatch so that the accused may opt to avail the statutory defence.
The Court held that the accused had been deprived of a valuable right statutorily available to him.

On this view of the matter,
the court did not allow the criminal complaint to proceed against the accused.
We have cases under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 involving the same question.

In this connection reference be made to decisions of this Court in State of Haryana v. Brij Lal Mittal & Ors., [1998] 5 SCC 343 under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940; Municipal Corporation of Delhi v.
Ghisa Ram, AIR (1967) SC 970; Chetumal v. State of Madhya Pradesh & Anr., DA vs Chander Kumar etc [1981] 3 SCC 72 and Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf & Anr., [1999] 2 SCC 400 all under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf & Anr., [1999] 2 SCC 400
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It cannot be gainsaid, therefore, that the respondents in these appeals have been deprived of their valuable right to have the sample tested from the Central Insecticides Laboratory under sub- section (4) of Section 24 of the Act.

Under sub-section (3) of Section 24 report signed by the Insecticide analyst shall be evidence of the facts stated therein and shall be conclusive evidence against the accused only if the accused do not, within 28 days of the receipt of the report, notify in writing to the Insecticides Inspector or the Court before which proceedings are pending that they intend to adduce evidence to controvert the report.
In the present cases Insecticide Inspector was notified that the accused intended to adduce evidence to controvert the report.
By the time the matter reached the court, shelf life of the sample had already expired and no purpose would have been served informing the court of such an intention.
The report of the Insecticide Analyst was, therefore, not conclusive.

A valuable right had been conferred on the accused to have the sample tested from the Central Insecticides Laboratory and in the circumstances of the case accused have been deprived of that right, thus, prejudicing them in their defence."
15.
Now in the present case, the sample of Kuber Readymade Scented Khaini was lifted on 08/08/202.
Form VI prepared on the spot shows that it was best before six months from the date of packing.
The complaint was filed in the court on 03/11/2003.
DA vs Chander Kumar etc Therefore it is clear that the complaint was filed in court after the period of its expiry and therefore convicting the accused in thses circumstances, will not be proper.

Therefore, placing reliance upon the aforesaid judgement of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Da vs Chander Kumar Etc on 16 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64226644/
6

sentences.text: Reliance may further be had upon the case titled as Food Inspector vs Banarsi Das & Ors 2014 (2) FAC 177 wherein the order of declining cognizance was uphold by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi when the complaint was filed after expiry period of the product more particularly when no preservative was added to the sample as per the prosecution evidence.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

Reliance may further be had on the judgement of Marico Ltd and others vs State of Delhi 2015 (1) FAC 40.
16.Regarding misbranding

entities.text: Marico Ltd and others vs State of Delhi 2015 (1) FAC 40
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , the defence has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in S.S. Gokul Krishanan & Others vs State 2009(1) FAC 132 to argue that there was a policy of the complainant department of 1985 numbered as Policy No F6(228)/85/ENF/PFA wherein a decision was taken to give a written warning to the first offenders.

entities.text: S.S. Gokul Krishanan & Others vs State 2009(1) FAC 132
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Although this policy was withdrawn by order No. 5/07 dated 14.09.2007 but since this case was filed May 2003, the accused are covered by aforesaid policy.

Although, no such policy has been placed or proved on record by other side and this policy was further withdrawn as per the aforesaid judgment on the ground that Section 20 of the PFA Act does not confer any such power on the consenting authority to DA vs Chander Kumar etc issue such warning to the vendors found violating Rule 32 of the PFA Act.

Be that as it may, PFA Act or Rules does not provide any such warning but since the benefit of this policy has been given in the case of S.S. Gokul Krishnan (referred above), I feel myself found by the ratio of that case.

Therefore as far as issue of misbranding is concerned, since, it is not the case of the prosecution that the accused were given earlier a warning and despite that they continued with the offence, the accused are given the benefit of this policy and therefore they shall not be liable for violation of Rule 24 and 42 of PFA Rules.

The judgment of Gokul Krishnan (supra) has also been followed in the judgment of M/s Bunge India Pvt Ltd & Others vs State & Another Crl.MC 439/2008 dated 20.01.2011.
17.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the basis of aforesaid discussions, the accused are acquitted from this case.
